scope: Documented configuration and observable behavior, not undisclosed implementation. Independent checks and example prompts are proposed exercises; none was executed against a live AWS account.

devops.title: AWS DevOps Agent
devops.status: Documented operational mechanisms; controls and learning schedules are feature-specific. Managed-agent UI availability may vary by rollout.
devops.opening: A recurring alarm does not prove that its previous root cause has returned. Use historical context to select hypotheses, then test those hypotheses against current telemetry. The documentation describes retained Markdown knowledge, routing by descriptions, and a managed learning process. It does not document a customer-operated model-training switch.
devops.learning: Historical investigations → managed learning runs → versioned memory → relevance-based retrieval → a new investigation. User instructions, selected skills and tool permissions remain separate controls.

records.title: Recall recurring alarm causes
records.activation: Automatic learning; inspect and activate stores
records.mechanism: The learning agent summarizes earlier investigations into monitor-specific memory. At a new session, store descriptions are exposed first; relevant entries are fetched selectively rather than injecting every incident. Memory versions retain change history.
records.prerequisites: An Agent Space with investigation history and connected evidence sources.
steps: Open Knowledge → Memories. Inspect the monitors store and its Active setting.
Open a monitor entry and review its evidence and versions. Use the store or entry toggle to allow or exclude recall.
Open Agents → Managed agents → Learning to inspect available history. Custom-agent attachment is a separate step; see D-M03.
records.scope: Current guidance: daily monitor-memory refresh when investigations exist in the preceding two weeks; a monitor memory without updates for two weeks can be removed. Full stores evict the oldest item.
records.control: Use memory/store toggles to stop recall. Chat can request a correction or deletion. Managed refresh may later regenerate relevant content.
records.limits: A previous cause is a hypothesis, not a finding about the current incident. The guide does not describe model-weight training.
checks: In a non-production Agent Space, select a resolved incident whose cause was independently confirmed.
Record its alarm identity, evidence links and memory version. Start a separate investigation using new evidence, not a duplicate event.
Compare the agent’s cited past context with current logs. A matching conclusion alone is not proof that memory was read.
records.artifact: Investigation IDs, memory/store identifier, version and timestamp, retrieved evidence, reviewer decision.
records.fallback: When no memory is present, inspect recent learning activity and store activation; use the approved incident record explicitly and label the manual context.
records.example: Illustrative: “For this staging alarm, compare current evidence with relevant prior causes. Cite what was recalled and list disconfirming signals. Do not change resources.”
slide_setup: Inspect the monitor entry and versions.
Check Active state and Learning history.
records.slide_mechanism: The learning agent summarizes earlier investigations into monitor-specific memory.
records.slide_boundary: Deactivate stale or incorrect context. Use memory/store toggles to stop recall.

records.title: Refresh environment and tool-use knowledge
records.mechanism: Environment, repository, pipeline and tool-use knowledge is maintained as managed memory. Older learned-skill entries move to Memories on their next refresh; no manual conversion is required.
records.prerequisites: Connected resources and integrations; recent completed investigations for activity-based refresh.
steps: Open Knowledge and inspect the learned item. If it still appears under Skills, follow its migration state rather than creating a duplicate.
Use Topology → Regenerate, or request a refresh in chat.
Inspect the versioned summary in the console Summary report or web-app Artifacts.
records.scope: Environment understanding refreshes after discovery and relevant integration changes. Current memory guidance describes activity-gated refreshes and a separate tool-use threshold; exact cadence is not a delivery-time guarantee.
records.control: Managed-agent schedules belong to the service. Use supported regeneration and knowledge controls rather than inventing a cron override.
records.limits: Cached documentation differs on historical refresh thresholds. This guide does not use a numeric threshold as an acceptance criterion.
checks: Compare one service-to-repository link with deployment configuration.
Check the memory version after an authorized refresh; do not infer completion merely from clicking Regenerate.
Audit one tool-use recommendation against a successful tool result and its permissions.
records.artifact: Before/after knowledge versions, changed integration, a sampled dependency and supporting configuration.
records.fallback: Keep a reviewer-approved topology snapshot as explicit context; investigate permission or discovery gaps before trusting the generated map.
records.example: Illustrative: “Refresh the environment understanding and report which version is now available. Distinguish observed dependencies from inferred relationships.”
slide_setup: Review the new summary and version.
records.slide_mechanism: Environment, repository, pipeline and tool-use knowledge is maintained as managed memory.
records.slide_boundary: Refresh is not continuous retraining. Managed-agent schedules belong to the service.

records.title: Attach retained context to a custom agent
records.mechanism: A custom agent can read attached memory stores and write to attached custom stores. Managed stores are read-only to custom agents. A newly created custom agent has no memory access until stores are attached.
records.prerequisites: An Agent Space with an integration, a custom agent and relevant stores.
steps: Create a store through Knowledge → Memories → Create memory store; describe its subject and when it should be used.
Create or edit the custom agent and select the Memory stores field, or ask Chat to attach a named store.
Configure MCP tools separately through Chat; attaching knowledge does not grant a tool.
records.scope: Attachment is per custom agent, within its Agent Space. Managed chat and custom-agent write behavior must not be conflated.
records.control: Remove an attachment in the agent’s configuration when the job no longer needs that context.
records.limits: Permission to read retained knowledge does not authorize infrastructure changes. Description matching does not guarantee recall on every run.
checks: Run a read-only task with a non-sensitive synthetic fact in an attached custom store.
Compare the result with an otherwise equivalent agent without that attachment.
Confirm the custom agent cannot treat managed history as its own editable store.
records.artifact: Agent definition, store attachment list, test prompt, output and invocation ID.
records.fallback: Pass the fact explicitly for this run and record the missing attachment; do not broaden all tools to solve a context problem.
records.example: Illustrative: “Attach staging-service-notes to the weekly-review agent. Permit only the tools needed to read investigations.”
slide: Test with a synthetic scoped fact
slide_setup: Create a described custom memory store.
Attach it in the custom-agent definition.
records.slide_mechanism: A custom agent can read attached memory stores and write to attached custom stores.
records.slide_boundary: Tools and memory are separate. Remove an attachment in the agent’s configuration when the job no longer needs that context.

records.title: Apply always-on agent instructions
records.mechanism: Global and agent-specific AGENTS.md content is loaded for new sessions. Both scopes apply when relevant. An instruction update does not replace the content already loaded in an in-progress session.
records.prerequisites: Agent Space administration access and a reviewed instruction change.
steps: Open a managed agent’s Agent definition.
Edit Global instructions for space-wide guidance, or Agent instructions for that agent type.
Save; global changes require confirmation. Start a new session to assess the revision.
records.scope: Global scope affects the Agent Space; specific scope affects that managed agent type.
records.control: Download a copy before replacing or deleting instructions. Restore approved text through the editor when rolling back.
records.limits: Instructions are prompt context, not an IAM permission boundary or a guarantee that every requested behavior will occur.
checks: Set a harmless output requirement and verify it in a new session.
Check that an existing session is not being used to test a newly saved instruction.
Keep a negative authorization test separate from the instruction test.
records.artifact: Reviewed AGENTS.md revision, scope, approver, test session and resulting artifact.
records.fallback: Use explicit run-scoped instructions while investigating propagation; retain access restrictions in IAM.
records.example: Illustrative instruction: “Distinguish observed facts, hypotheses and missing evidence. Identify the source window for each operational claim.”
slide_setup: Save; evaluate in a new session.
records.slide_mechanism: Global and agent-specific AGENTS.md content is loaded for new sessions.
records.slide_boundary: Guidance does not grant access. Download a copy before replacing or deleting instructions.

records.title: Load a procedure through a skill
records.availability: Documented; this guide uses document-only skills
records.mechanism: A skill packages instructions and references. The name and description guide relevance selection; agent-type targeting limits where it is offered.
records.prerequisites: An Agent Space and an approved procedure. This example requires no executable skill content.
steps: Choose Knowledge → Skills → Add skill → Create skill.
Enter a specific name, applicability description and Markdown procedure; select intended agent types and Active status.
For packaged references, use the documented ZIP import with a root SKILL.md and required frontmatter.
records.scope: Skills are procedural context. They differ from informational memory and always-on instructions.
records.control: Edit the skill or set it Inactive to prevent use for new work.
records.limits: The skill page contains differing script-upload wording and a Sandbox-preview exception. Do not assume executable skill support from this document-only example.
checks: Use one task matching the description and one clearly unrelated task.
Inspect whether the expected procedure and evidence requests appear.
Review reference freshness; a well-formed skill can still contain an incorrect procedure.
records.artifact: SKILL.md version, selected agent types, activation state and matched/unmatched test results.
records.fallback: Provide the approved procedure explicitly for the current run; improve its description rather than adding unrelated instructions.
records.example: Illustrative procedure: compare deployment time, application errors and dependency health before selecting a cause.
records.slide_mechanism: A skill packages instructions and references.
records.slide_boundary: No execution assumed for documents. Edit the skill or set it Inactive to prevent use for new work.

records.title: Discover resources without confusing scope with access
records.mechanism: Topology discovery uses CloudFormation and, for tagged non-CloudFormation resources, AWS Resource Explorer. Observability and deployment data contribute relationships. Investigation can use accessible resources outside the displayed graph. For investigation sessions, effective permissions intersect the account role with the service-applied session policy; adding an IAM permission outside that policy does not make it usable.
records.prerequisites: Configured account connections and appropriately scoped roles; Resource Explorer enabled where its discovery is needed.
steps: Verify the connected primary and source accounts.
Enable Resource Explorer in a target account when tagged resources outside CloudFormation must be discovered.
Inspect Topology. Restrict the account role to enforce actual access boundaries.
records.scope: Graph inclusion describes context, not authorization. IAM is the access boundary.
records.control: Change role permissions to restrict access; removing a graph item alone is not sufficient.
records.limits: An absent node may indicate discovery or telemetry gaps, not absence of the deployed resource. Directed actions use a separate opt-in execution path; see D-M09.
checks: Compare a CloudFormation resource and an externally deployed tagged resource against inventory.
Confirm an out-of-scope resource is inaccessible under the role, even if named in chat.
records.artifact: Account/Region scope, sampled resource identifiers, role policy review and discovery comparison.
records.fallback: Use current inventory as explicit context; resolve missing indexing or account permissions before accepting completeness.
records.example: Illustrative: “List which checkout resources were discovered and which evidence sources are missing. Do not treat the topology as an access policy.”
slide_setup: Restrict the account roles in IAM.
records.slide_mechanism: Topology describes resource context. Effective investigation permissions intersect account-role policy with the service-applied session policy.
records.slide_boundary: Enforce access in IAM. Change role permissions to restrict access; removing a graph item alone is not sufficient.

records.title: Trigger investigations through authenticated events
records.mechanism: An external HTTP event can enqueue an investigation. Generic webhooks support HMAC or bearer-token authentication; delivery acceptance does not prove that an investigation started.
records.prerequisites: An Agent Space, an authorized event sender and secure storage for the generated credential.
steps: Open the Agent Space Capabilities tab and add a generic webhook.
Select HMAC or API key, save the one-time credential securely and configure the sender using the documented schema.
Send a controlled event with a unique incident ID and current timestamp; inspect the investigation, not only HTTP status.
records.scope: Credentials belong to the webhook. Duplicate events can be deduplicated.
records.control: Rotate the credential through the webhook editor and update the sender; removing the webhook stops that endpoint.
records.limits: Never include secrets in sample payloads. A successful HTTP response means queued processing, not a completed analysis.
checks: Use a non-production event and trace sender ID to investigation ID.
Confirm malformed or unauthorized requests do not become accepted work.
Record rotation readiness without deliberately exposing production credentials.
records.artifact: Redacted event, sender time, request result and investigation ID/status.
records.fallback: Open the investigation manually with the same bounded context while fixing authentication, schema or deduplication issues.
records.example: Illustrative payload fields: incidentId, title, service, timestamp, current symptom and links to authorized evidence.
slide: HTTP success is not analysis success
records.slide_mechanism: An external HTTP event can enqueue an investigation.
records.slide_boundary: HTTP success is not analysis success. Rotate the credential through the webhook editor and update the sender; removing the webhook stops that endpoint.

records.title: Schedule a bounded custom-agent job
records.mechanism: A custom agent can run on demand or through a schedule. Each invocation has a history entry and recorded tool activity. The managed learning schedule is a different, service-owned mechanism.
records.prerequisites: A custom agent with only the required tools, skills and stores.
steps: Open the custom agent and use Run Now to validate its configuration.
In Triggers, create a Schedule and provide the documented cron or rate expression.
Inspect the listed next-run time and the invocation History after execution.
records.scope: Each invocation uses the configured custom-agent scope. A schedule is not a broader permission grant.
records.control: Review or remove the schedule through trigger management when no longer needed; do not assume removing a future trigger cancels an active invocation.
records.limits: Report generation requires suitable source access and an explicit output definition. No completion-time guarantee follows from the schedule.
checks: Use a daily read-only staging review with a narrow time window.
Confirm the actual run time, tools used and output completeness.
Verify no unexpected external publication occurred.
records.artifact: Agent revision, schedule expression and timezone interpretation, invocation trace, report and owner.
records.fallback: Run the approved task on demand, or perform the review manually, until scheduled execution is verified.
records.example: Illustrative: “Summarize completed staging investigations for the last day. Retain unresolved evidence gaps. Do not create tickets.”
slide: Do not alter managed learning schedules
slide_setup: Define and test the custom agent.
Create a schedule and bounded prompt.
records.slide_mechanism: A custom agent can run on demand or through a schedule.
records.slide_boundary: Do not alter managed learning schedules. Review or remove the schedule through trigger management when no longer needed; do not assume removing a future trigger cancels an active invocation.

records.title: Authorize mutating directed actions
records.mechanism: Directed actions require an enabled Agent Space, an elevated account role or tool configuration, and operator approval for the specific mutation. The role is a permission ceiling; execution is further scoped.
records.prerequisites: Authorized administrators and operators; a deliberately restricted elevated role for the target account.
steps: Enable directed actions in Agent Space settings.
Register the target account’s elevated role; follow the documented trust policy and action restrictions.
Review the proposed operation, resource, parameters and rollback before approving a single action.
records.scope: Read-only investigation remains available without elevated access. Tool classifications and roles are not memory settings.
records.control: Disable directed actions at the Agent Space to remove elevated capability. Approved execution is attributable in CloudTrail.
records.limits: The API preferences update replaces the supplied preference map; preserve other settings. Do not infer that all AWS operations are supported.
checks: Use a reversible staging change only after separate authorization.
Check the approved operation and resource against CloudTrail and actual state.
Reject a deliberately out-of-scope proposal; confirm no mutation occurred.
records.artifact: Approval identity, operation/parameters, role scope, audit event and rollback verification.
records.fallback: Keep the investigation read-only and hand the reviewed change to the normal deployment process.
records.example: Illustrative: “Describe the proposed staging change and rollback. Request approval before any mutation.”
records.slide_mechanism: Directed actions require an enabled Agent Space, an elevated account role or tool configuration, and operator approval for the specific mutation.
records.slide_boundary: Remembered context grants no authority. Disable directed actions at the Agent Space to remove elevated capability.

use_case.title: Test recall without assuming the old cause has returned
use_case.preflight: Use a non-production Agent Space with a resolved, independently reviewed incident and a distinct new investigation. Keep directed actions disabled. Use prepared records if no managed memory is yet available.
steps: Scope the comparison
Name the old incident, a new symptom window and the read-only resource boundary.
Incident owner
Two distinct investigation IDs and an agreed evidence window.
D-M06
Inspect retained knowledge
Inspect Knowledge → Memories for the relevant monitor and its versions.
Operator
Entry is relevant, active and traceable to the reviewed incident.
D-M01
Check the consumer
For a custom agent, explicitly attach the chosen store.
Agent administrator
Correct store attached; no unrelated tool access added.
D-M03
Start a separate investigation
Ask for current evidence and disconfirming observations.
Operator
New task, current data and a record of recalled context if observable.
D-M01
Challenge the conclusion
Compare proposed cause with telemetry; do not count a matching narrative as proof of recall.
Service reviewer
Independent evidence supports or rejects the hypothesis.
D-M02
Correct or exclude stale knowledge
Update or deactivate an incorrect item and retain the review record.
Knowledge owner
Correction recorded and assessed in a new session.
D-M01
use_case.exit: Accept only when the new conclusion is supported by current evidence and the retained context is correctly scoped. Record recall as unproven when no read evidence is available.
use_case.fallback: Use a prepared memory record and investigation trace. Do not wait for the managed learning schedule during a live session.

kiro.title: Kiro
kiro.status: IDE, CLI and Web have different controls. Local memory requires supported versions; Web features retain their own availability and plan restrictions.
kiro.opening: Separate facts discovered during coding from rules the team intentionally maintains. Local memory can retain a debugging lesson; steering expresses maintained conventions; skills provide procedures; hooks and MCP enable actions. No one control replaces the others.
kiro.learning: Local IDE/CLI memory retains selected context on the same machine. Web can incorporate the task creator’s review feedback. Neither statement establishes a shared memory store across local clients, cloud agents and teammates.

records.title: Retain debugging context in local memory
records.surface: IDE ≥1.4.0; CLI ≥2.29.0 in local V3 sessions
records.availability: Documented 20 October 2026 release; off by default
records.mechanism: Kiro can extract and refine selected context, then retrieve it for later tasks. Local memories are shared by IDE and CLI on the same machine and can be repository-scoped or global; they are not full conversation copies.
records.prerequisites: A supported client version and a trusted local workspace for memory changes.
steps: IDE: open Memories in the activity bar, then settings, and choose Use and learn.
CLI: open /memories → config, select read & write and enable automatic memory updates when desired.
Start a new CLI session after changing access. Use /memories → list to inspect entries.
records.scope: Local storage is not documented as automatic synchronization to Kiro Web or other team members.
records.control: IDE supports inspection and deletion; CLI supports read only/off modes and chat-based corrections when writable. Access changes apply to a new CLI session.
records.limits: Recalled text consumes context. Capture and recall do not guarantee correctness or update model weights as a user-controlled operation.
checks: Record a harmless repository-specific prerequisite, then inspect the saved entry and its scope.
In a new session, ask for the relevant test plan and look for an explicit Memory read in the transcript.
Correct the fact and test again; check that an unrelated repository does not inherit repository-only advice.
records.artifact: Client versions, memory mode, repository scope, entry before/after correction and recall evidence.
records.fallback: Keep the approved fact in version-controlled steering when automatic retention is absent or unsuitable; do not enable broad access merely to obtain recall.
records.example: Illustrative: “Remember for this training repository that integration tests require the local test fixture. This is a test convention, not a credential.”
slide: Enable memory in IDE or CLI
slide_setup: Select Use and learn or read & write.
Inspect entries; test a fresh session.
records.slide_mechanism: Kiro can extract and refine selected context, then retrieve it for later tasks.
records.slide_boundary: Not shared cloud/team memory. IDE supports inspection and deletion; CLI supports read only/off modes and chat-based corrections when writable.

records.title: Use the task creator’s Web review feedback
records.availability: Web feature; separate from local memory
records.mechanism: Kiro Web responds to review feedback and can carry the task creator’s guidance into future work. The steering guide limits this learning to the user who created the task, not other reviewers.
records.prerequisites: A connected repository and a Web task created by the reviewing user.
steps: Connect GitHub in Web settings and grant only required repositories.
Create a bounded task and review its proposed change.
Add a specific review correction from the task creator’s account; inspect the resulting revision and later behavior.
records.scope: This is a Web feedback mechanism. The reviewed guides do not establish shared storage with local IDE/CLI memory.
records.control: Use checked-in steering for rules requiring explicit team ownership and version control. A dedicated Web memory-delete control is not established by these pages.
records.limits: Commenting does not authorize merging or deployment. Avoid treating every reviewer’s comment as persistent policy.
checks: Use a small formatting or error-handling correction in a disposable repository.
Compare the changed PR and a later task; label a behavioral match as observation, not proof of an undocumented storage implementation.
records.artifact: Task creator, PR/comment link, revision diff and later task result.
records.fallback: Put the reviewed rule in repository steering and provide it explicitly; record the uncertainty about implicit feedback retention.
records.example: Illustrative: “Use the existing request-ID propagation helper instead of creating a new helper.”
slide: Review and comment on the task PR
records.slide_mechanism: Kiro Web responds to review feedback and can carry the task creator’s guidance into future work.
records.slide_boundary: No local-memory synchronization assumed. Use checked-in steering for rules requiring explicit team ownership and version control.

records.title: Maintain explicit project guidance in steering
records.surface: IDE / CLI / Web, with surface-specific scope
records.availability: Documented; custom-agent inclusion must be configured
records.mechanism: Workspace steering lives in .kiro/steering; local global steering lives in ~/.kiro/steering. Inclusion modes control when guidance is loaded. The cloud cannot read the local global directory.
records.prerequisites: Repository access and an approved guidance file; correct client-specific configuration.
steps: Create a Markdown steering file with a clear applicability statement.
Choose the documented inclusion mode for the client; use workspace scope for repository-owned conventions.
For a custom agent, explicitly include steering in its resources configuration. Upload local global guidance through Configuration Sync when it is required in cloud sessions.
records.scope: Workspace guidance takes priority over conflicting local-global guidance. Steering is explicitly maintained text, unlike inferred memory.
records.control: Edit or remove the file through normal review; verify the new context in a fresh session.
records.limits: Steering content is not a sandbox, access-control policy or substitute for tests.
checks: Check a matching and a nonmatching task for a conditional instruction.
Inspect the custom-agent resources rather than assuming default-agent behavior carries over.
records.artifact: Guidance file revision, inclusion mode, client/surface and test transcript.
records.fallback: Attach the approved guidance explicitly while correcting inclusion or sync settings.
records.example: Illustrative: “When changing request-ID handling, preserve the public header contract and add a regression test.”
slide: Test inclusion on the actual client
records.slide_mechanism: Workspace steering lives in .kiro/steering; local global steering lives in ~/.kiro/steering.
records.slide_boundary: Text guidance is not authorization. Edit or remove the file through normal review; verify the new context in a fresh session.

records.title: Load a reusable procedure through Agent Skills
records.mechanism: Kiro first discovers a skill’s name and description, then loads instructions when relevant; scripts and references can be loaded as needed. This is procedure selection, not learned incident memory.
records.prerequisites: A reviewed skill package and appropriate permissions for any actions it describes.
steps: Place a SKILL.md package in .kiro/skills/<name>/ with name and description frontmatter.
Keep supporting references in the package and describe the tasks that should activate it.
For global local use, use ~/.kiro/skills; verify cloud availability separately.
records.scope: Package contents can include executable material. Read the package before enabling it.
records.control: Remove or revise the package through the repository’s change process.
records.limits: Skill activation does not validate its content or authorize every script it references.
checks: Choose a read-only procedure and inspect the loaded skill when the task matches.
Verify any command uses the intended working directory and least required permissions.
records.artifact: Skill package revision, activation evidence, command log and reviewed result.
records.fallback: Use the reviewed steps manually when activation is uncertain; do not accept a successful-looking narrative without command results.
records.example: Illustrative skill: inspect existing request-ID entry points and report missing propagation tests without changing code.
records.slide_mechanism: Kiro first discovers a skill’s name and description, then loads instructions when relevant; scripts and references can be loaded as needed.
records.slide_boundary: Scripts need separate review. Remove or revise the package through the repository’s change process.

records.title: Run event-driven hooks with an explicit effect
records.surface: IDE / CLI; not Web or Mobile
records.mechanism: Kiro hooks run a shell command or inject an agent prompt when a configured event occurs. Standalone v1 JSON files allow the same event definition to be used by local IDE and CLI clients.
records.prerequisites: An applicable local client, repository tooling and a reviewed command or prompt.
steps: Create .kiro/hooks/<name>.json using version v1 and the documented hooks array.
Select a supported trigger and matcher; start with a non-mutating validation command.
Migrate older formats using the client’s documented migration flow, then inspect the resulting configuration.
records.scope: An agent-prompt action and a blocking command hook are not equivalent. File patterns and event semantics are client-specific.
records.control: Remove or revise the hook file and confirm it is no longer loaded; avoid broad event matchers.
records.limits: A hook can run code automatically. Do not use unreviewed scripts or commands downloaded at invocation time.
checks: In a disposable repository, trigger one matching file event and one unrelated event.
Check the actual command exit result and side effects; guard against repeated-trigger loops.
records.artifact: Hook JSON revision, matching event, command output, exit status and changed-file list.
records.fallback: Disable the hook and run the validation command manually until trigger behavior is understood.
records.example: Illustrative task: run an already-installed test check after a relevant local file event; do not install dependencies as part of the hook.
slide: Configure a v1 hook and matcher
Check exits and actual side effects
Prompt hooks are not access controls
slide_setup: Create a supported v1 hook file.
records.slide_mechanism: Kiro hooks run a shell command or inject an agent prompt when a configured event occurs.
records.slide_boundary: Prompt hooks are not access controls. Remove or revise the hook file and confirm it is no longer loaded; avoid broad event matchers.

records.title: Expose tools through MCP with controlled approval
records.surface: Local IDE / CLI configuration; cloud setup differs
records.mechanism: MCP adds tool interfaces from a local process or remote server. Configuration and tool approval are separate from the text that tells the agent how to use a tool.
records.prerequisites: A reviewed MCP server, suitable authentication and the installed client’s supported transport.
steps: Use .kiro/settings/mcp.json for workspace configuration or the user-level equivalent.
Configure the server endpoint/process without hard-coded credentials; leave autoApprove empty for initial evaluation.
Save, inspect available tools, and approve or deny the requested operation after reviewing its arguments.
records.scope: Workspace configuration can override user configuration. Local filesystem configuration does not imply that a cloud session has the same credentials.
records.control: Use disabled or disabledTools to remove exposure; review any autoApprove changes as a permission decision.
records.limits: Connecting a server is not proof that its data is trustworthy. Do not auto-approve all tools to fix a failed read.
checks: Choose one read-only tool, record its input and compare its output with the source system.
Deny a write request and verify the external system did not change.
records.artifact: Redacted config, server identity, exposed tool list, approval decision and external result.
records.fallback: Disable the server; obtain the evidence through an approved read-only path.
records.example: Illustrative: “Retrieve the documented configuration of this test resource. Do not perform any write operation.”
records.slide_mechanism: MCP adds tool interfaces from a local process or remote server.
records.slide_boundary: Instructions do not confer credentials. Use disabled or disabledTools to remove exposure; review any autoApprove changes as a permission decision.

records.title: Run a repository task on a Web schedule
records.availability: Eligible paid plans; Web availability applies
records.mechanism: A Web automation runs a prompt against selected repositories in autonomous mode on a schedule. When changes are produced, the review artifact can be a pull request.
records.prerequisites: An eligible plan, connected repositories and a prompt with bounded output.
steps: Open Automations in the Web sidebar and create the automation.
Specify its name, prompt, repositories and schedule; review the configuration.
Inspect a run and its output; use the row status or Edit screen to disable future runs.
records.scope: Scheduling is a Web mechanism, separate from local hooks and local memory.
records.control: Disable or delete the automation to stop future scheduled runs.
records.limits: A scheduled task is not permission to merge or deploy. Completion time depends on the work; inspect failures rather than inferring success from a schedule.
checks: Start with a report-only task in a test repository.
Confirm repository selection, schedule interpretation and resulting session.
Check that a disabled automation does not start a subsequent scheduled run.
records.artifact: Automation definition, run/session link, output or PR and responsible reviewer.
records.fallback: Perform the same task manually while resolving plan access or execution failures.
records.example: Illustrative: “Summarize merged request-ID changes in the last review window. Do not edit repository files.”
slide: Not a local hook or merge approval
slide_setup: Inspect a run and its review artifact.
records.slide_mechanism: A Web automation runs a prompt against selected repositories in autonomous mode on a schedule.
records.slide_boundary: Not a local hook or merge approval. Disable or delete the automation to stop future scheduled runs.

records.title: Separate reference retrieval from session compaction
records.surface: CLI knowledge bases / supported session commands
records.activation: Explicit indexed sources; automatic or manual summary
records.mechanism: A configured CLI knowledge base indexes selected reference material for retrieval. Compaction instead summarizes older conversation content within an existing task; it is not proof that durable memory was saved.
records.prerequisites: A current custom-agent profile and approved local documents for a knowledge base.
steps: Configure a knowledgeBase resource using the documented source, name and indexing options.
Use autoUpdate only when re-indexing on agent start is intended.
Use /compact to summarize a long conversation; preserve critical evidence outside the conversation.
records.scope: Indexed files, current-session summaries and cross-session memories have different sources and lifecycles.
records.control: Remove the knowledge-base resource to stop offering that index. Correct source files and rebuild rather than editing a summary as if it were source truth.
records.limits: A summary may omit details. Do not use it as the only retained incident record or infer full-text retention.
checks: Change one non-sensitive reference fact, refresh the index and ask for its source.
After compaction, verify the current goal and next action still match the approved task.
records.artifact: Source revision, profile configuration, retrieval citation and before/after task-state checklist.
records.fallback: Reattach the authoritative document and restate the active task if retrieval or compaction loses essential context.
records.example: Illustrative: “Find the request-ID contract in the indexed project documents and identify the file revision. Do not substitute an older conversation summary.”
slide: Check cited revision and task state
records.slide_mechanism: A configured CLI knowledge base indexes selected reference material for retrieval.
records.slide_boundary: Compaction is not persistent learning. Remove the knowledge-base resource to stop offering that index.

use_case.title: Verify opt-in memory on a local development client
use_case.preflight: Use a disposable repository, supported IDE/CLI versions and a harmless preference. Avoid secrets, personal data and production tools.

Check supported version and whether memory is off, read-only or read/write.

Select Use and learn in the IDE or set the CLI memory read/write configuration.

Inspectable memory entry with the correct scope.

Test a fresh session
Ask a task that would need the fact without restating it.

Separate session and observable entry use where available.

Keep policy explicit
Move mandatory team convention into reviewed steering rather than relying solely on inferred memory.

Version-controlled guidance with deliberate inclusion.

Correct and disable

security.title: AWS Security Agent / AWS Continuum
security.status: Penetration testing is generally available. Code review, design review and threat modeling are documented as preview; check feature and Region access before setup.
security.opening: Additional Learning Resources are application inputs, not evidence of a cross-incident training mechanism. A penetration test can use source code and design information, validate findings, propose repairs and rerun selected checks. Each stage has a different authorization and acceptance boundary.
security.learning: Updated application context → scoped assessment → evidence and findings → reviewed/deployed repair → targeted revalidation. No configurable cross-run incident-memory switch was identified in the reviewed guidance. This is an evidence limitation, not a claim about undisclosed internals.

records.title: Supply application context for a scoped test
records.mechanism: Additional Learning Resources supply source and application documents to the assessment. This is task context; the reviewed guidance does not identify it as a persistent incident-memory control.
records.prerequisites: An enabled Agent Space, authorized and verified target, and permission to provide the selected application materials.
steps: Create a penetration test and define the target and exclusions.
At Additional Learning Resources, select connected resources or upload the relevant material.
Confirm the selected revision and network access needed by connected sources before starting.
records.scope: Test-selected context may contain source, API or design information. Connected sources can expose updated versions on subsequent use.
records.control: Change selected resources for the next test. Use integration and repository access controls to restrict the available material.
records.limits: Adding context does not authorize out-of-scope testing or establish cross-run model training.
checks: Use a staging target and a non-sensitive application note with a traceable revision.
Inspect test context and coverage against that revision; verify the deployed application matches it.
records.artifact: Target authorization, resource selection, revision identifiers, exclusions and test ID.
records.fallback: Exclude an unavailable source and record the coverage limitation; do not widen target access to resolve a document problem.
records.example: Illustrative context: a sanitized API description identifying a staging endpoint and the test roles permitted to use it.
slide: Context is not a learning toggle
records.slide_mechanism: Additional Learning Resources supply source and application documents to the assessment.
records.slide_boundary: Context is not a learning toggle. Change selected resources for the next test.

records.title: Authenticate a test without expanding its scope
records.activation: Explicit test credentials or advanced credential flow
records.mechanism: Authentication lets the assessment reach authorized application behavior. The guide distinguishes direct credentials from advanced flows using IAM, Secrets Manager and Lambda.
records.prerequisites: Owner authorization, test identities with bounded privileges, valid login behavior and approved secret handling.
steps: Open the authentication configuration for the test.
Choose the documented credential method; configure the login target and instructions where required.
Verify the test account and its allowed roles before launching the assessment.
records.scope: The credential method grants application access only within the intended test scope; network connectivity and target exclusions remain separate.
records.control: Revoke or rotate the test identity after the exercise. Stop the test if observed activity exceeds authorization.
records.limits: Credentials do not belong in steering, persistent memory, exported evidence or this repository.
checks: Sign in with the test identity through an approved manual check.
Confirm both an allowed operation and a forbidden operation; inspect test logs for authentication failures.
records.artifact: Redacted authentication method, test role, allowed operations, login check and revocation record.
records.fallback: Pause the test and repair the authorized credential flow; label unauthenticated coverage as incomplete.
records.example: Illustrative: configure a staging-only reviewer account with no billing, administrative or production privileges.
records.slide_mechanism: Authentication lets the assessment reach authorized application behavior.
records.slide_boundary: Never retain secrets as memory. Revoke or rotate the test identity after the exercise.

records.title: Validate and review reported findings
records.mechanism: The service uses deterministic checks where possible and independent replay in other cases. Results distinguish validated findings from lower-confidence or unverified candidates.
records.prerequisites: A completed or progressing authorized assessment and access to its results.
steps: Open the penetration-test results and inspect the finding evidence.
Review confidence, reproduction material and coverage, not just severity.
Inspect unverified candidates separately where the interface permits; do not silently promote them to confirmed defects.
records.scope: A finding relates to the tested application state and selected scope.
records.control: Keep active-test monitoring and stop responsibility with the authorized operator.
records.limits: Validation does not prove complete security coverage. A missing finding is not proof that a defect is absent.
checks: Have an authorized reviewer reproduce a selected finding safely in staging.
Compare the request, identity, application version and impact with the report.
records.artifact: Finding ID, evidence, confidence, affected version, reproduction decision and unresolved coverage.
records.fallback: Classify the finding as unresolved when reproduction or evidence is insufficient; do not convert uncertainty into a pass.
records.example: Illustrative review: distinguish an observed access-control violation from a hypothesis inferred from source code.
slide: No finding is not an assurance claim
records.slide_mechanism: The service uses deterministic checks where possible and independent replay in other cases.
records.slide_boundary: No finding is not an assurance claim. Keep active-test monitoring and stop responsibility with the authorized operator.

records.title: Maintain security requirements as explicit policy context
records.activation: Enable a managed or custom requirement pack
records.mechanism: Requirement packs define criteria used during design and code reviews. They are shared across Agent Spaces, not a private memory of one application.
records.prerequisites: Access to security-requirement administration and an approved applicability definition.
steps: Open Security requirements and select a managed pack or create a custom pack.
For a custom requirement, define applicability, compliance criteria and remediation guidance.
Enable the pack and run a new review to evaluate the change.
records.scope: Pack changes affect new reviews, not existing review results. Managed requirements are read-only.
records.control: Disable a pack to exclude it from new reviews; preserve the approved custom definition before editing.
records.limits: Uploading new source documents regenerates the pack and replaces existing requirements, including manual entries. Framework packs do not certify compliance.
checks: Use one applicable example and one deliberately not-applicable example.
Check the reported requirement identifier and retain the pack revision used for the review.
records.artifact: Pack and requirement IDs, applicability, revision, review ID and reviewer decision.
records.fallback: Keep a manually reviewed policy checklist while resolving pack applicability; do not reuse an old review as evidence of a new pack.
records.example: Illustrative policy: authenticated service endpoints must enforce ownership checks; explicitly exclude public health endpoints.
slide: Create or enable a requirement pack
Test a new review against applicability
slide_setup: Choose or create a requirement pack.
Enable it and run a new review.
records.slide_mechanism: Requirement packs supply criteria for new design and code reviews. They are shared across Agent Spaces, not private incident memories.
records.slide_boundary: Regeneration replaces pack contents. Disable a pack to exclude it from new reviews; preserve the approved custom definition before editing.

records.title: Enable proposed code repair per repository
records.surface: Agent Space repository configuration / finding detail
records.availability: Capability availability follows the originating review or test
records.activation: Administrator enablement, then a finding repair request
records.mechanism: Repository remediation produces a proposed change for review. For the private GitHub path used here, the artifact is a pull request; other source providers can return different artifacts.
records.prerequisites: Enabled testing or code review, an authorized GitHub App registration and the relevant private repository.
steps: Open the Agent Space Penetration test tab and choose the GitHub registration, or edit its Code review repository entry.
In the repository-capability wizard, enable Automatic remediation for the selected repository and choose Connect.
From a supported finding, request remediation and inspect the resulting change.
records.scope: The setting is repository-specific. It does not authorize merging or deployment.
records.control: Review or disable the repository remediation setting when no longer needed; keep branch protection independent.
records.limits: A proposed repair may be incomplete or introduce regressions. An open PR is not evidence that the running application is fixed.
checks: Match the finding to changed lines and inspect the PR scope.
Run regression and security checks independently before any approved merge.
records.artifact: Finding-to-PR link, repository setting, commit IDs, test evidence and human review decision.
records.fallback: Implement a reviewed manual repair when the repository or finding is unsupported; retain the original evidence.
records.example: Illustrative: request a repair for a confirmed staging access-control finding, without allowing auto-merge.
slide_setup: Request repair of a supported finding.
records.slide_mechanism: Repository remediation produces a proposed change for review.
records.slide_boundary: PR creation is not deployment. Review or disable the repository remediation setting when no longer needed; keep branch protection independent.

records.title: Revalidate a deployed repair
records.mechanism: Revalidation repeats checks for selected findings against the running target. It creates a separate job and does not replace the original finding record.
records.prerequisites: A completed test, selected findings, a deployed candidate fix, reachable target and valid test authentication.
steps: Deploy the reviewed repair to the originally authorized environment.
Select findings in the completed test and choose revalidation.
Review the new job status and evidence against the deployed version.
records.scope: This is targeted checking of known findings, not a new assessment for unrelated vulnerabilities.
records.control: Keep the original test record and the subsequent verification record; authorization remains scoped to the target.
records.limits: Resolved means the issue was not reproduced by that check. It is not an exhaustive assurance statement.
checks: Record the deployed commit and verify target/authentication health before interpreting the result.
Distinguish a negative reproduction from an unreachable target or failed test.
records.artifact: Original finding, deployed commit, revalidation job, result evidence and residual risk.
records.fallback: Mark verification inconclusive if the target or credentials fail; repair the test conditions before rerunning.
records.example: Illustrative: revalidate one repaired staging finding after deployment, with no expansion of the original scope.
records.slide_mechanism: Revalidation repeats checks for selected findings against the running target.
records.slide_boundary: Not a fresh discovery scan. Keep the original test record and the subsequent verification record; authorization remains scoped to the target.

records.title: Connect an IDE scan through the Security Agent MCP server
records.availability: Code review and threat-model review are preview
records.activation: Install the supported integration; authorize first-use provisioning
records.mechanism: The MCP integration packages code, uploads it to an account S3 bucket, starts a scan and retrieves findings. First use can provision an Agent Space, IAM role and bucket.
records.prerequisites: Configured AWS credentials with the documented setup and scan permissions; supported client and package runtime.
steps: Install the AWS Security Agent Power in Kiro, following the official IDE integration procedure.
Review the AWS profile, Region and setup permissions before first use.
Request a scan of a disposable repository and inspect the created resources and findings.
records.scope: Source leaves the local machine. A differential scan can still upload full repository context with its diff.
records.control: Review installed hooks and MCP tools; remove or disable the integration when access is no longer approved.
records.limits: The AWS integration page and current Kiro configuration guide show different manual config paths. Prefer the supported Power setup and inspect the installed configuration rather than copying an older path. No runtime guarantee is assumed.
checks: Check the packaged source for secrets and unnecessary content before upload.
Confirm bucket, role, scan ID and source revision; inspect generated fixes before committing.
records.artifact: Redacted integration config, provisioned resources, source manifest, scan result and reviewer decision.
records.fallback: Use the documented console or repository review flow while resolving client-version differences.
records.example: Illustrative: scan a small synthetic repository containing no credentials or customer data, without requesting fixes.
slide: A diff scan can upload full context
records.slide_mechanism: The MCP integration packages code, uploads it to an account S3 bucket, starts a scan and retrieves findings.
records.slide_boundary: A diff scan can upload full context. Review installed hooks and MCP tools; remove or disable the integration when access is no longer approved.

use_case.title: Carry application evidence through repair and revalidation
use_case.preflight: Use an owned staging application and explicit test authorization. Have a completed finding and a prepared deployed-fix result; do not wait for a full penetration test.
steps: Fix the authorization boundary
Identify the test target, identities, exclusions and stop owner.
Application owner
Written scope and approved test roles.
S-M02
Identify the application inputs
Select context at a known source and deployment revision.
Security engineer
Context-to-target revision match.
S-M01
Review one finding
Inspect evidence, confidence and reproducibility.
Security reviewer
Safe reproduction or an explicit inconclusive result.
S-M03
Inspect remediation setup
Check per-repository enablement and inspect the proposed repair.
Repository administrator
Finding-linked PR, no merge implied.
S-M05
Verify the deployed version
Use the normal change process and confirm the staging commit.
Release owner
Independent tests and deployed revision recorded.
S-M05
Revalidate and record residual risk
Review the targeted revalidation job and original finding together.
Security reviewer
Reachable target, correct identity and evidence for the result.
S-M06
use_case.exit: The finding, proposed code change, deployed version and revalidation result are linked. “Not reproduced” is not rewritten as complete security assurance.
use_case.fallback: Use previously authorized prepared results and label the demonstration as a walkthrough; no test runs against an unapproved target.

finops.title: AWS FinOps Agent
finops.status: The service and all mechanisms in this guide are preview. Data access depends on the configured IAM role; external writes have action-specific approval behavior.
finops.opening: A cost explanation combines retrieved account data, maintained organization files and remembered preferences or corrections. A remembered explanation is not a newly verified cost driver. Reconcile the data window and cost basis each time before acting on an interpretation.
finops.learning: Conversation corrections and investigation outcomes can become agent-specific memory. Uploaded context supplies maintained organization definitions. Scheduled or event-triggered tasks use that context but do not confer permission to resize infrastructure.

records.title: Establish the agent identity and data boundary
records.activation: Separate agent role and operator access
records.mechanism: An agent has its own IAM role, context, memory, tasks and artifacts. Account-data visibility follows the configured role; another agent is not a shared-memory extension.
records.prerequisites: Preview access and permissions to create the required roles and operator access.
steps: Create the agent in the console and select or create its agent role.
Configure the operator web-application role and optional integrations.
Review the wizard settings and verify access from the intended operator identity.
records.scope: Content is isolated between agents. Storage and cross-region processing have a separately documented US data-location boundary.
records.control: Change role policies and integrations through the administrative configuration; do not treat a chat instruction as an access restriction.
records.limits: A broad data role can expose more than the displayed report scope. Missing permissions can produce incomplete analysis.
checks: Compare an allowed cost query with an intentionally unavailable data source.
Record the agent identity and confirm the operator is not accidentally using another agent.
records.artifact: Agent ID, role policies, operator scope, approved data-location assessment and test results.
records.fallback: Use a manually scoped cost export while resolving access; do not grant administrator access for convenience.
records.example: Illustrative: create a report-only evaluation agent using a narrowly scoped role and no external publishing integration.
slide: Separate agents do not share context
records.slide_mechanism: An agent has its own IAM role, context, memory, tasks and artifacts.
records.slide_boundary: Separate agents do not share context. Change role policies and integrations through the administrative configuration; do not treat a chat instruction as an access restriction.

records.title: Supply maintained organization context
records.mechanism: Uploaded context supplies owner mappings, categories, report structures and instructions. The agent reads this material but cannot edit or delete the files through chat.
records.prerequisites: Approved non-sensitive context and authorized users of the agent.
steps: Open Context files and upload a focused supported file.
Use a new question to check the mapping or instruction.
Maintain the file in the workspace when organization definitions change.
records.scope: Files are available to users with access to the agent and used by its work.
records.control: Delete removes a file from active context by soft deletion; Restore reactivates it.
records.limits: Do not upload personal or sensitive information. An owner mapping is not an IAM policy.
checks: Use a synthetic account-to-team mapping and verify a sampled attribution.
Check for conflicting old context before accepting the result.
records.artifact: Context filename, approved revision, sampled mapping and verification output.
records.fallback: Provide the approved mapping explicitly for a single task and label the missing maintained context.
records.example: Illustrative file: a synthetic account identifier mapped to a team alias, without personal contact details.
slide: Soft deletion is not full erasure
records.slide_mechanism: Uploaded context supplies owner mappings, categories, report structures and instructions.
records.slide_boundary: Soft deletion is not full erasure. Delete removes a file from active context by soft deletion; Restore reactivates it.

records.title: Retain and correct preferences across sessions
records.activation: Natural-language remember, update and forget requests
records.mechanism: Memory can retain preferences, corrections and task outcomes for later sessions. This differs from an uploaded context file and from the summary of one long conversation.
records.prerequisites: A configured agent and non-sensitive facts appropriate to retain.
steps: Ask the agent to remember a specific reporting preference or correction.
Start a separate conversation and check its use.
Request an update or forgetting of that specific entry when it is no longer valid.
records.scope: Memory belongs to the agent, not to every agent in the account.
records.control: Use the documented chat controls for memory; do not assume forgetting deletes earlier conversation records.
records.limits: A remembered cause must be rechecked against current data. No separate model-training switch is established by these instructions.
checks: Use a harmless synthetic reporting preference, not a secret.
Test correction in a new session; retain the original data query for reconciliation.
records.artifact: Memory request, agent ID, independent new-session output and correction record.
records.fallback: Provide the preference explicitly and record that cross-session recall was not demonstrated.
records.example: Illustrative: “Remember that this evaluation uses unblended costs grouped by Region. Treat prior investigation conclusions as hypotheses.”
slide: Ask to remember, update or forget
Memory does not replace current data
records.slide_mechanism: Memory can retain preferences, corrections and task outcomes for later sessions.
records.slide_boundary: Memory does not replace current data. Use the documented chat controls for memory; do not assume forgetting deletes earlier conversation records.

records.title: Create bounded on-demand and scheduled tasks
records.activation: Explicit task request or recurring automation
records.mechanism: On-demand, scheduled and event-based work share a task queue. A task is created when requested; a normal cost question can remain an interactive answer.
records.prerequisites: An accessible agent, required data permissions and a bounded output definition.
steps: Ask to create a task, or open Tasks → Create tasks.
For recurrence, describe the schedule and output in chat.
Inspect the created automation, its task history and destination before relying on it.
records.scope: Each trigger creates a task. Execution duration is distinct from the schedule and from presentation demo time.
records.control: Disable or delete the automation to stop future triggers. Cancel a running task from its detail page where supported.
records.limits: External publishing behavior must be reviewed separately; a task may carry more effects than a read-only report.
checks: Start with report generation and no Jira or Slack destination.
Verify schedule interpretation, task state and artifact completeness.
records.artifact: Task or automation definition, schedule, task IDs, artifact and acceptance decision.
records.fallback: Run the query interactively and retain a manual report while investigating task errors.
records.example: Illustrative: “Create a task to reconcile last month’s service costs using the approved cost basis. Produce a report; do not publish externally.”
slide_setup: Request a task or use Create tasks.
records.slide_mechanism: On-demand, scheduled and event-based work share a task queue.
records.slide_boundary: Cancel work separately from triggers. Disable or delete the automation to stop future triggers.

records.title: Route cost anomaly events to an investigation
records.mechanism: A Cost Anomaly Detection event starts a matching automation through an EventBridge managed rule. The agent then runs the configured investigation and destination action.
records.prerequisites: An anomaly monitor, the required EventBridge permissions and an approved destination connection.
steps: Register Slack at account level, then bind the selected channel to the agent with Add connection.
In chat, specify the monitor or threshold, investigation and destination.
Open Automations and inspect the COST_ANOMALY trigger, status and associated tasks.
records.scope: The automation reacts to matching monitor events; it does not independently replace Cost Anomaly Detection.
records.control: Disable or delete the automation to stop new tasks. Existing task records remain.
records.limits: Slack delivery is not gated by per-message approval. Automatic Jira writes are pre-authorized during setup.
checks: Use an authorized test destination and inspect the exact monitor/threshold.
Trace a matching event to a task and delivery record without deliberately generating unnecessary spend.
records.artifact: Monitor, rule/automation identity, task ID, query evidence and destination result.
records.fallback: Investigate an existing anomaly on demand and label the missing event-routing evidence.
records.example: Illustrative: configure a staging evaluation monitor to send findings only to an approved test channel.
slide: Trace event to task and delivery
slide_setup: Configure a monitor and EventBridge access.
records.slide_mechanism: A Cost Anomaly Detection event starts a matching automation through an EventBridge managed rule.
records.slide_boundary: Setup can pre-authorize external writes. Disable or delete the automation to stop new tasks.

records.title: Apply action-specific publishing controls
records.activation: Different approval behavior by action and origin
records.mechanism: Interactive or on-demand Jira issue/comment actions require confirmation. Scheduled and event-based Jira actions are pre-authorized. Slack posting does not require approval, including interactive use.
records.prerequisites: An approved integration and a destination appropriate for the data.
steps: Inspect the Jira project or Slack channel connection.
For interactive Jira, review the displayed action details before confirming.
For automation, review the entire publishing instruction before enabling it.
records.scope: This is not a universal human-approval layer and is not authorization to resize infrastructure.
records.control: Remove or restrict integrations and disable automations when publishing is no longer approved.
records.limits: A prompt saying “ask first” should not be substituted for the product’s documented action controls.
checks: Test interactive Jira refusal/confirmation with a disposable issue.
Verify automation and Slack publishing only in approved test destinations.
records.artifact: Action type, invocation origin, destination, approval or pre-authorization record and delivery evidence.
records.fallback: Disable external publishing and retain the report for manual review.
records.example: Illustrative: generate a cost finding locally in the agent first, then separately authorize a disposable Jira issue.
slide: Approval depends on action and origin
slide_setup: Review publishing before enabling a schedule.
records.slide_mechanism: Interactive or on-demand Jira writes require confirmation. Automated Jira writes are pre-authorized at setup; Slack posting has no approval prompt.
records.slide_boundary: Slack has no approval prompt. Remove or restrict integrations and disable automations when publishing is no longer approved.

records.title: Separate retained data from session summarization
records.mechanism: Long conversations can be summarized to fit the model context window. Persistent memory, files, conversation history, tasks and artifacts have different lifecycles; an ephemeral runtime does not imply ephemeral records.
records.prerequisites: An owner for retained agent data and a documented removal procedure.
steps: Identify whether the unwanted item is context, memory, an artifact, a task or conversation history.
Use the specific deletion, forgetting, cancellation or automation control.
For categories without individual deletion during preview, evaluate whole-agent deletion with the owner.
records.scope: Conversation and task records can remain until agent deletion; soft-deleted context can be restored.
records.control: Whole-agent deletion removes the interaction data and web-app link according to the documented lifecycle; review dependencies first.
records.limits: Do not equate a summary, a forgotten fact, a disabled automation and complete data removal.
checks: Check that disabled automation stops new tasks while historical tasks remain.
Confirm removal behavior in a disposable agent before using it as a retention procedure.
records.artifact: Data category, requested operation, responsible owner, retained residual records and verification result.
records.fallback: Escalate retention requirements that the preview controls cannot satisfy; do not claim deletion based on an empty chat.
records.example: Illustrative: remove a synthetic preference, disable its reporting automation and document which history is still retained.
slide: Context and history have different lifecycles
Ephemeral runtime does not mean no retention
records.slide_mechanism: Long conversations can be summarized to fit the model context window.
records.slide_boundary: Ephemeral runtime does not mean no retention. Whole-agent deletion removes the interaction data and web-app link according to the documented lifecycle; review dependencies first.

use_case.title: Retain a reporting correction without accepting stale cost analysis
use_case.preflight: Use a preview evaluation agent and synthetic preferences. Keep external publishing disconnected until separately approved.
steps: Establish the data contract
State date window, cost basis, currency, filters and agent identity.
FinOps reviewer
Repeatable query definition.
F-M01
Load maintained context
Upload a sanitized team mapping and inspect a sample.
Context owner
Mapping revision and correct attribution.
F-M02
Remember a preference
Request a reporting-format preference, not an unsupported root-cause conclusion.
Operator
Specific memory request retained.
F-M03
Test a new session
Check the preference and reconcile the cost result independently.
FinOps reviewer
New session plus source totals.
F-M03
Inspect any automation effects
Review schedule/event trigger and Jira/Slack destination behavior.
Integration owner
Action-specific approval boundary recorded.
F-M06
Correct or remove the test data
Forget the preference and remove active context where appropriate.
Data owner
Residual history acknowledged.
F-M07
use_case.exit: The retained preference is correctly used, the cost numbers reconcile, and any publication is separately authorized. No savings outcome is asserted.
use_case.fallback: Use synthetic data and a prepared task history; do not generate cloud spend to trigger a demonstration.

comparison: DevOps Agent
Managed investigation/environment memory; attached custom stores
Managed learning plus explicit store controls
Knowledge → Memories; custom-agent attachments
Current investigation evidence; inspect versions
No customer model-training switch established
Kiro
Local memory; explicit steering; Web creator feedback
Local memory opt-in; instructions and tools separately configured
Memories panel or /memories; repository files; Web settings
Separate session, scoped entry and code/test evidence
No assumed local↔Web or team-memory synchronization
Security Agent
Selected application resources; explicit requirements; finding/revalidation records
Per-test inputs; per-pack and repository settings
Test setup; Security requirements; repository wizard
Safe reproduction; deployed revision; revalidation job
No cross-incident memory toggle identified in reviewed pages
FinOps Agent
Uploaded organization files; conversational memory; task history
Context upload; remember/update/forget; explicit automation
Context files; chat; Tasks and Automations
Current cost query and reconciliation; inspect destination effects
Remembered outcomes are not fresh cost evidence
controls: Record whether context is local-machine, repository, Agent Space, individual agent or task-specific. Never infer a portfolio-wide store.
Instructions and memory affect what is considered. IAM, application credentials and tool approvals determine what can be accessed or changed.
Record the selected feature, setting, attachment, client version and first new session or job used to test it.
Use retained context to form a hypothesis, not to prove it. Reconcile with current telemetry, tests, reproduced findings or billing queries.
A disabled trigger, removed attachment, forgotten fact and deleted history are different outcomes. Test the documented control for the actual data category.
Store official source, review date, surface and unresolved discrepancy. Treat a changed configuration path or migration as a reason to recheck before rollout.
evidence_notes: Incident learning is used here only for the documented retention and reuse of knowledge. It is not a claim that tenant incidents fine-tune model weights. Service-improvement data use is a separate policy question.
DevOps learned-skills guidance is migrating to managed memory. Current and cached official pages differ; confirm the live UI and avoid relying on historical numeric refresh thresholds.
Kiro local memory is documented in the dated 20 October 2026 release. Older cached pages describing IDE support as forthcoming must not override that dated release.
The Security Agent IDE guide and current Kiro guide differ on manual MCP paths. This guide uses the supported Power installation and requires inspection of the actual client configuration.
Executable DevOps skills have a preview exception alongside older restrictive wording. Only document-only DevOps skills are prescribed here.
Feature-specific Region, plan, role and preview constraints must be checked in the linked guide before enabling a mechanism. This extension is not a new audit of every historical capability record.
